proof.text: Use the Zariski-etale quasi-coherent equivalence to write $\mathcal I=F_{\mathrm{et}}$ for a quasi-coherent Zariski module $F$, with its specified open-section normalization. On every etale $V\to T$ its restriction is $(a^*F)_{\mathrm{et}}$. For affine $U\to T$, affine etale acyclicity gives $H^1(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal I|_U)=0$. Apply the long exact sequence of the underlying additive sheaves, using the Ext/derived comparison and the natural degree-zero identification with sections. It gives $0\to\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal A(U)\to\mathcal O_U(U)\to0$. In particular the restriction to Zariski opens is an exact sequence of sheaves: the quotient is surjective on an affine open basis, and kernels are computed sectionwise. The same argument applies on every etale $V$. No $\mathcal O_T$-module structure on $\mathcal A$ is asserted or needed.

Fix an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset T$ and put $R=\mathcal A(U)$ and $K=\mathcal I(U)$. Step 1 identifies $B=R/K$, with $K^2=0$. Every prime of $R$ contains $K$, since $k^2=0$ implies $k$ belongs to every prime. Taking inverse images and quotients therefore gives inverse bijections between primes of $B$ and $R$. They identify $D_B(\overline r)$ with $D_R(r)$ for every $r\in R$; these sets are bases of the respective Zariski topologies. Thus $|U|\simeq|\operatorname{Spec}R|$ canonically.

source.place: Tag 05YV (lemma-first-order-thickening), affine case: homeomorphism of underlying spaces

proof.text: For $r\in R$ put $W=D_B(\overline r)$. It is affine, with ring $B_{\overline r}$. The image of $r$ in $\mathcal A(W)$ is a unit: lift the inverse of $\overline r$ using step 1, and correct the resulting product $1+k$ by multiplying by $1-k$, since $k^2=0$. Hence restriction gives $R_r\to\mathcal A(W)$. Localize $0\to K\to R\to B\to0$ at $r$; exactness of localization makes its row short exact. Compare it with the section row of step 1 on $W$. The right comparison is $B_{\overline r}\simeq\mathcal O_U(W)$. For the left comparison, the quasi-coherent equivalence and the affine pullback-section formula identify $K_r=K\otimes_B B_{\overline r}\simeq\mathcal I(W)$ by $k/r^n\mapsto\overline r^{-n}k|_W$. Thus the short five lemma, applied to the underlying additive groups, makes $R_r\to\mathcal A(W)$ a ring isomorphism. All maps are restriction maps and inverses to powers of $r$, so these isomorphisms commute with restrictions between principal opens.

source.place: Tag 05YV (lemma-first-order-thickening), affine comparison, written on principal opens instead of stalks

proof.text: The principal-open structure-sheaf formula for $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and step 3 give a ring-sheaf isomorphism $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\simeq\mathcal A|_{U_{\mathrm{Zar}}}$ over the homeomorphism of step 2: extend the compatible basis maps to any open by sheaf gluing. Thus $(U,\mathcal A|_U)$ is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The identifications agree on overlaps because their maps are the original restrictions of $\mathcal A$; one can cover an overlap by affine opens without assuming the overlap itself affine. These local identifications show directly that $(|T|,\mathcal A|_{T_{\mathrm{Zar}}})$ is a scheme. Its quotient to $\mathcal O_T$ defines the identity-on-points closed immersion by the definition of closed immersion; its kernel has square zero sectionwise. Taking $U=T$ proves both affine assertions.

source.place: Tag 05YV (lemma-first-order-thickening), conclusion from the affine comparisons

proof.text: Apply steps 1--4 to the restriction of the extension on every etale $V\to T$. For a morphism $h:V\to W$ over $T$, the restriction maps of the original site sheaf give on Zariski opens a map $h^{-1}(\mathcal A|_{W_{\mathrm{Zar}}})\to\mathcal A|_{V_{\mathrm{Zar}}}$. Together with $|h|$ it is a morphism of locally ringed spaces: in each stalk the quotient by its square-zero ideal is the original local ring of $V$ or $W$, and an element is a unit exactly when its residue is a unit (lift an inverse and use $(1+k)^{-1}=1-k$). Localness therefore follows from localness of the stalk map of $h$. Identity and composition equations hold on every section because they hold for the restrictions of $\mathcal A$. This constructs the functor $V\mapsto V^+$ and the commutative squares of thickenings.

Let $U\subset T$ be affine and $V\subset a^{-1}U$ affine. Set $R=\mathcal A(U)$, $S=\mathcal A(V)$, $B=\mathcal O_T(U)$, $C=\mathcal O_V(V)$, $K=\mathcal I(U)$ and $L=\mathcal I(V)$. These are exact square-zero section extensions by step 1. The quasi-coherent equivalence and the affine pullback-section formula identify the canonical map $K\otimes_B C\to L$ with $k\otimes c\mapsto c\,k|_V$, and it is an isomorphism. The scheme maps $V\to U$ and $V^+|_V\to U^+$ are $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the restriction maps $B\to C$ and $R\to S$, morphisms into affine schemes being determined by global sections (steps 4 and 5 identify $V^+|_V=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $U^+=\operatorname{Spec}R$). Since $a$ is etale, target locality makes $a^{-1}U\to U$ etale and source locality, for the open cover $\{V,a^{-1}U\}$ of $a^{-1}U$, makes $\operatorname{Spec}C=V\to U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ etale; this is the hypothesis of the criterion in its stated form. Apply the square-zero ring-extension criterion to conclude $R\to S$ is etale. Also $L=KS$: every tensor is a finite sum of $k\otimes c$, and $c$ lifts to $S$ by step 1. Thus $S\otimes_R B=S/KS=S/L=C$, and since the fibre product of affine spectra is the spectrum of the tensor product with the canonical projections, the affine square is consequently cartesian, with the canonical maps, not just abstractly isomorphic rings.

For each affine open $U\subset T$, cover $a^{-1}U$ by affine opens $V$. Their thickenings are exactly the corresponding opens of $V^+$ and $T^+$, since both constructions use the same topological spaces and restricted sheaves. Step 6 and source locality show $(a^+)^{-1}(U^+)\to U^+$ is etale; target locality then shows $a^+$ is etale. The cartesian identifications of step 6 agree on overlaps, being induced by the already constructed arrows. Gluing their inverses gives $V\simeq V^+\times_{T^+}T$, so the entire square is cartesian.

Pullback along $T\hookrightarrow T^+$ is an equivalence of small etale sites. By step 7, the functor already constructed is its inverse on objects and arrows: each $V^+$ pulls back canonically to $V$, and full faithfulness supplies the unique compatible comparison with any other lift. The transported structure sheaf has value $\Gamma(V^+,\mathcal O_{V^+})=\Gamma(|V|,\mathcal A|_{V_{\mathrm{Zar}}})=\mathcal A(V)$, and its maps are precisely the original restriction maps by step 5. This is an isomorphism of the entire ring sheaf, not merely its restriction to Zariski opens. Its quotient and kernel agree sectionwise with the original ones. Joint surjectivity of lifted families follows also from the unchanged spaces and point maps. Finally pullback preserves the finite fibre products of etale schemes, and its full faithfulness reflects the universal properties of the lifted diagrams; hence the inverse construction preserves all the stated finite fibre-product diagrams.

title: Scheme charts of square-zero extensions on the small etale site
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. On its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] let $0\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal O_T\to0$ be an exact sequence of sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], where $\mathcal A$ is a sheaf of commutative unital rings, its last map is a ring homomorphism, and its kernel is an ideal with square zero and is quasi-coherent with its quotient $\mathcal O_T$-action [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. The locally ringed space $T^+=(|T|,\mathcal A|_{T_{\mathrm{Zar}}})$ is a scheme; the quotient defines a closed immersion $T\hookrightarrow T^+$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with square-zero ideal and the same underlying topological space. For affine $T$ it is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(T)$ and $\mathcal A(T)\to\mathcal O_T(T)$ is surjective. For every etale scheme map $a:V\to T$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], restrict this extension to $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ and form $V^+$ in the same way. The ring-sheaf restriction maps give an etale map $a^+:V^+\to T^+$, functorially for identities and composition, and the square with $V\to T$ and the two closed immersions is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. These maps identify the sheaf $\mathcal O_{T^+}$, transported along the equivalence of small etale sites given by pullback along the thickening $T\hookrightarrow T^+$ [sbc-lem-thickening-etale-site], with the entire sheaf $\mathcal A$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, compatibly with the quotient, the kernel, and etale restrictions. Jointly surjective etale families and finite fibre-product diagrams of etale $T$-schemes are preserved by this construction.
